key_insight: Large language models can nearly match expert raters and outperform laypeople when judging empathic communication across multiple evaluation frameworks, but their accuracy hinges on having clear, specific scoring criteria.
problem_solved: Evaluating empathic communication is time-consuming, costly, and inconsistent across raters; this paper tests whether LLMs can provide reliable, scalable assessments comparable to experts.
method: Compare ratings from LLMs, domain experts, and laypeople on multiple empathic-communication frameworks and sample interactions.
Measure inter-rater reliability and agreement with expert judgments across conditions, including varying specificity of evaluation criteria.
Analyze how rubric clarity and prompt design affect LLM and human rater reliability.
impact: Shows LLMs can be a practical, scalable tool for assessing empathy in communication when paired with well-defined rubrics—enabling faster evaluation pipelines and broader deployment in research and applied systems.
visual_elements: Bar chart comparing inter-rater reliability (LLMs vs experts vs laypeople) across frameworks
Two-panel diagram showing 'Unclear vs Clear Criteria' and resulting change in rater agreement
Flowchart of the evaluation pipeline: data → rubric/prompt → rater types → reliability metrics
Icon set representing expert, layperson, and LLM to quickly convey comparative performance
paper_title: When large language models are reliable for judging empathic communication
paper_authors: Aakriti Kumar, Nalin Poungpeth, Diyi Yang, Erina Farrell, Bruce L. Lambert
